newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to give Dole the Medal of Freedom.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to give Dole the Medal of Freedom.

text.p: President Clinton will present former Republican rival Bob Dole with the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian award, administration officials said Wednesday.
Dole is scheduled to receive the award on Friday during a White House ceremony honouring veterans of World War II. Dole was wounded while fighting in Italy.

While declining to confirm or deny the decision to present Dole with the award, Deputy White House Press Secretary Mary Ellen Glynn said, "It sounds like an excellent way to pay tribute to a person who has devoted his life to public service."
Dole resigned in June as Senate Republican leader in order to concentrate full-time on his unsucessful challenge to deny Clinton a second term in the White House.
Clinton, who intends to stress a theme of healing when he delivers his inaugural address on Monday, wanted to honour the 73-year-old Dole's public service to the nation.

Dole was wounded as a U.S. Army second lieutenant in Italy 50 years ago as he led an assault on a German machinegun nest. After a lengthy recovery from his wounds, he entered politics and won a House of Representatives seat in 1960 and a Senate seat in 1968.
